question: What belongs in Appearance, and what belongs in Effects?
context: A rectangle today shows an Appearance panel and an Effects panel, and it is not clear what belongs in which. Both appear to carry an opacity and a blur. The strips in the brief draw the same rectangle under each answer, carrying two borders (one inside the edge, one outside) and a shadow.

options.label: Appearance is what it IS, Effects is what you ADD
options.summary: Two panels, split on one rule anyone can state. Appearance holds the things every shape simply has, always in the same order: opacity, fill, outline, and a corner radius only where there are corners. Effects starts empty and grows: press the plus for a border, a shadow, a glow, a blur. You can add the same kind twice, so two borders with different offsets give you an inner one and an outer one. A part's settings sit behind a line of their own, so a shadow's blur can never read as the layer's blur.
pros: The rule is one sentence, so you never wonder which panel a thing is in
Two borders, two shadows, a glow and a blur all become the same move
Nothing is named twice: Blur under Effects is only ever an effect you added
A new shape starts with a short, quiet panel
cons: Blur and corner radius change homes, so a habit has to be relearned once
Two panels means two places to look when you are hunting for something you set earlier
options.mitigation: The order inside Appearance is fixed and short, so the hunt is always the same four rows; anything else you set, you added, and added things are in Effects.

options.label: One panel, no line to learn
options.summary: No second section at all. Everything the layer wears is in one list called Appearance: what it always has at the top, what you added underneath, with one plus on the header. There is no rule about which panel a thing lives in, because there is only one panel.
pros: Nothing to learn and nothing to remember: one place, one plus
One less section header eating room in the dock
Impossible to look in the wrong panel
cons: One long list mixes what a shape always has with what you chose to add
Nothing to collapse: today you can shut Effects and keep Appearance open
With two shadows the list is already long enough to scroll
options.mitigation: The always-there rows stay pinned at the top in a fixed order, so the added ones never push them about.

options.label: Change nothing but the ownership
options.summary: The two panels stay exactly as they are. The only change is a line down the left of a part's settings, so a shadow's Blur, Size and Opacity are visibly the shadow's and never read as the layer's. No second border, no move for blur or corner radius.
pros: The smallest change that fixes the thing you actually reported
cons: Appearance still carries an added shadow, so the split you asked for is not made
Still nowhere to put a second border
Effects still holds three sliders that are not effects anybody added
options.mitigation: It can be a first step: the ownership line is needed under any of these three.
